title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation fraud carried out with a synthetic video call. The fraudsters presented a fabricated likeness of a public figure over WhatsApp and used it to make a financial offer, then extracted payments by layering on fees and penalties. The failure sits at the point of contact between a victim and an unverified identity, not inside any system the victim had chosen to trust.

Nothing in the reporting shows how the video was produced or what tooling was used. It also does not establish whether the platform detected or acted on the call. Catching this would have required the victim to independently verify that the person on the call was who he appeared to be, through a channel other than the one the call arrived on.

The case was registered under the Information Technology Act and is described as the first deepfake case of this kind reported in the city. That a case was registered is not a finding of guilt against any person, and the identity of the callers is not established in the reporting.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri lost over Rs 1.04 lakh to fraudsters who used a deepfake video call to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The callers promised him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid, then demanded fees for exchange charges, a locked PIN, and a fake CBI fine. Giri paid through a digital payment app before refusing a further Rs 50,000 demand and realizing he had been cheated.

Giri contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then the Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. This is the first such deepfake case reported in the city. Police urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on similar claims.
